entries.definition: A stochastic neural-network layer that masks individual weights and biases during training, so each example is processed through a randomly selected subset of the layer’s connections.
entries.identity_notes: This record denotes the original fully connected DropConnect layer and its training/inference conventions. Dynamic connection masking differs from dropping activation units, removing whole residual branches, masking spatial blocks and permanently pruning a weight matrix. The surrounding feature extractor and classifier are not part of the layer identity. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 276 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 5 and 5 lines respectively. Every text hit was a prior candidate lead or a closely related variant lead. Nine exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and three native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The original layer uses per-example masks, including biases. Shared minibatch masks, unmasked biases, inverted training rescaling and later structured weight-masking variants are not silently substituted for this source version.

Gaussian moment matching is an approximation to the finite Bernoulli sum; averaging sampled nonlinear activations is also approximate. Passing an averaged activation through a nonlinear downstream network is not exact averaging of full network predictions. Applying the activation to the mean generally differs from averaging activations.

The equal-mask paragraph uses 1/|M| while also describing 2^|M| masks. Exact averaging requires normalized mask probabilities; the record follows the weighted expectation in Equation4 rather than propagating that inconsistent displayed factor. No full proof audit of the source’s generalization bound is claimed.

Dense connection-mask storage and sampling can be costly; dynamic sparsity alone does not guarantee faster execution. Fully connected-layer evidence does not establish arbitrary convolutional/recurrent implementations, universal generalization improvement or a calibrated Bayesian posterior. No benchmark result or author code execution is asserted.

claims.statement: For each training example, draw independent Bernoulli keep masks for the layer’s weights and biases with a chosen retention probability p. Multiply the parameters elementwise by this mask, compute the affine preactivation and apply the nonlinear activation. Backpropagate through the masked connections, using the same mask for the weight gradients and for gradients passed to earlier layers. The original inference procedure approximates each preactivation by a Gaussian matched to the masked weighted sum’s mean and variance: p times the ordinary weighted sum, and p(1−p) times the sum of squared weight-input products, including the constant input used for bias. Draw samples from these Gaussians, apply the activation to each sample and average the resulting activations before passing them to the next layer. The paper’s sample count and p=0.5 experiments are configuration choices.

entries.name: Stochastic depth
entries.definition: A residual-network training procedure that randomly bypasses residual transformations during training and uses all residual transformations with survival-probability scaling during inference.
entries.identity_notes: This record covers the original 2016 stochastic-depth procedure with a block-survival draw per minibatch and test-time residual scaling. It is a training procedure for residual networks, not the residual architecture itself. Modern per-example drop-path functions, inverted scaling conventions and learned dynamic-depth methods require separate version assessment. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 276 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 5 and 5 lines respectively. Every text hit was a prior candidate lead or a closely related variant lead. Nine exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and three native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Identity bypass is conditional on the skip path and activation: a post-addition ReLU clips negative skip values, and a dimension-changing projection is not the same operation as an identity map. The procedure cannot be transferred to an arbitrary incompatible block by merely deleting its output.

The survival schedule in the core method varies with network depth, not automatically with elapsed training time. The paper’s final-block probability of0.5 is an experimental choice. Mini-batch sampling and inference scaling differ from later per-example or inverted-scaled implementations.

Survival-weighted inference is a practical combination of shared-weight subnetworks, not generally the exact expected prediction of the stochastic nonlinear network. Reduced expected active-block count does not by itself guarantee a proportional wall-clock saving; computation must actually be bypassed.

The source’s empirical gradient and benchmark observations do not certify absence of vanishing gradients, universal regularization improvement or arbitrarily deep trainability. No author code or trained network was executed.

claims.statement: Assign each residual block a survival probability and, for each training minibatch, sample whether to execute its residual transformation. An active block adds its residual output to the skip path before the architecture’s output activation; an inactive block bypasses the residual transformation while preserving the skip path. The source’s identity reduction relies on its nonnegative activations and compatible skip connection. It proposes a linear decrease in survival probability with block depth from an always-present input to a chosen last-block probability, while also considering a uniform assignment. The expected number of active residual blocks is the sum of their survival probabilities. During inference, activate every residual transformation and multiply its output by its training survival probability before adding the skip path. The original convention does not divide active training residuals by the survival probability.

entries.name: Zoneout
entries.definition: A recurrent-network regularization procedure that randomly preserves selected state components at their previous values instead of applying their proposed updates during training.
entries.identity_notes: Zoneout is a stochastic transition-modification procedure, not a particular RNN architecture or trained sequence model. Its identity branch retains previous activations; it differs from setting recurrent states to zero, dropping only input-gate contributions, fixed periodic update schedules and always skipping an entire recurrent layer. LSTM cells and hidden states can have separate preservation probabilities and masks. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 276 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Full-checkout fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files in worktree and main, returning 5 and 5 lines respectively. Every text hit was a prior candidate lead or a closely related variant lead. Nine exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms/comments and outgoing edges and three native neighboring mechanisms were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The generic operator formula in Section3.1 uses d for selecting the normal transition, whereas the LSTM formulas in Section3.2 use d for selecting preservation. The record defines its own preservation convention explicitly; those source masks are complements, not interchangeable symbols.

The printed LSTM hidden-state proposal uses the unzoned cell-update expression inside tanh. An implementation that instead uses the already-mixed cell state can differ when cell and hidden selectors differ. This general method record does not certify all LSTM code as equivalent or invent an uninspected implementation rule.

Replacing selectors by expectations gives a deterministic local mixture; nonlinear recurrence means it is not generally the exact ensemble-averaged state or output over complete stochastic trajectories. Preserved components pass their old values directly, but this does not guarantee that the entire network avoids vanishing/exploding gradients or processes every input in every component.

Very high preservation can suppress adaptation to new inputs. State/cell probabilities, sharing and other regularizers matter; the source’s task-specific results and conjectures do not establish universal improvement. No exact trained-model replication, parameter sweep or author-code execution is asserted.

claims.statement: At a recurrent timestep, form the model’s proposed next-state values and use a Bernoulli selector for each targeted component to choose between that proposal and its previous value. Defining z as the preservation probability, the update has the form mask times previous state plus one-minus-mask times proposed state, with a mask value of1 selecting preservation. This introduces direct identity paths through time for the preserved components. The source’s LSTM account usually uses separate selectors for memory cells and hidden states and also studies shared selectors. At testing, replace the random selector by its expectation, producing a weighted combination of previous and proposed values at each step. Selection probabilities, targeted state components and the underlying recurrent transition are configured choices; the procedure itself does not require a new learned gate.

definition.val: A regularization layer that applies Dropout to the input

comments: Applies Dropout to the input. The Dropout layer randomly sets input units to 0 with a frequency of rate at each step during training time, which helps prevent overfitting. Inputs not set to 0 are scaled up by 1/(1 - rate) such that the sum over all inputs is unchanged. Note that the Dropout layer only applies when training is set to True such that no values are dropped during inference. When using model.fit, training will be appropriately set to True automatically, and in other contexts, you can set the kwarg explicitly to True when calling the layer. (This is in contrast to setting trainable=False for a Dropout layer. trainable does not affect the layer's behavior, as Dropout does not have any variables/weights that can be frozen during training.)

native_neighbors.name: DropBlock
native_neighbors.definition: A training-time feature-map transformation for convolutional networks that suppresses randomly placed contiguous spatial blocks of activations and rescales retained activations.

claims.statement: During training, sample block seeds within the spatial region whose expanded square blocks fit inside the feature map, suppress the union of those blocks, multiply activations by the resulting keep mask and normalize using the observed retained-mask fraction. The paper uses a block size and a seed probability gamma computed approximately from the desired keep probability, block area and number of valid centers. Overlap makes the formula approximate. The author-linked pinned TensorFlow implementation confirms gamma as the probability that a valid center becomes a drop seed. It supports square feature maps, clamps block size to map width, expands zeros using minimum pooling, and computes normalization from the resulting mask tensor as a whole. During ordinary inference, the transformation returns its input unchanged. The paper recommends a linear decrease of keep probability from1 to a target during training; this schedule is an experimental choice rather than a new learned mask.

evidence.locator: Section3 and Algorithm1/Equation1, PDF pp.2–4; paper-linked implementation in Section4.1, PDFp.4; discussion PDFp.9
dropblock(), lines276–354: inference return, square-map constraint, seed_drop_rate, valid centers, block expansion and percent_ones normalization

aio_mappings.rationale: The method is represented as the defined neural-network component that transforms an input feature map for subsequent layers. The generic AIO Layer is broader than this particular transformation.

DropBlock shares stochastic training-time activation suppression with dropout. Its contiguous blocks, overlapping coverage and realized-mask normalization differ from the pinned independent-unit/fixed-rate description, so this is a related association rather than equivalence or a forced subclass claim.

limitations: Algorithm1 writes M~Bernoulli(gamma) while expanding zero entries, yet Equation1 and the pinned implementation use gamma as the drop-seed rate. These literal conventions differ under the usual Bernoulli success convention; the implementation resolves the convention used here without claiming an author-issued erratum.

The gamma expression does not guarantee the target retained fraction at every location or in every realization. Block overlap and edge coverage matter. The paper’s per-mask normalization and the pinned implementation’s whole-mask-tensor normalization should not be silently equated.

Both the displayed ratio and inspected code require a nonzero retained fraction; the inspected function has no all-zero-mask guard. Valid block sizes, probabilities, tensor shapes and numerical safeguards are implementation requirements, not consequences of the name DropBlock.

Random blocks are independent of a semantic object annotation and may remove useful information. The experiments with masking at inference are diagnostic perturbations, separate from the ordinary identity behavior. Reported architecture-specific gains and robustness do not establish universal benefits, and no author code or model was executed.

native_neighbors.name: Attention-based Dropout Layer
native_neighbors.definition: A training-time convolutional feature-map layer that stochastically applies either a thresholded spatial drop mask or sigmoid importance weights derived from channel-averaged activations, developed for weakly supervised object localization.

claims.statement: Average the input convolutional feature tensor over channels to obtain one spatial attention map. Set a threshold to a configured fraction gamma of that map’s maximum; construct a binary drop mask that suppresses positions above the threshold. Separately apply a sigmoid to the attention map to obtain importance weights. On a training iteration, choose the drop mask with the configured drop rate and otherwise choose the importance map, then multiply the selected spatial map into the input features across channels. These map operations add no trainable parameters; gradients through the importance branch train the surrounding classifier. ADL is disabled at testing and returns the feature map unchanged, without a train/test distribution compensation step. The source uses image-level classification labels and a separate heatmap extraction/localization procedure; ADL itself does not output an object bounding box.

evidence.locator: Section3, PDF pp.3–5 (printed2221–2223), and Figure1 on PDFp.2; failure-case discussion and Figure4, PDFp.8

aio_mappings.rationale: ADL is a specific input-to-output feature-map component inside a classifier, so the generic AIO Layer has broader scope.

ADL stochastically suppresses activations during training, which relates it to dropout. Its activation-dependent mask, alternative sigmoid branch and lack of the pinned fixed-rate dropout rescaling prevent identity or an unqualified subclass assertion.

limitations: The drop rate controls how often the drop-mask branch is selected, not the fraction of pixels removed. Thresholding depends on the activation distribution; the source prose specifies greater-than and less-than comparisons but leaves equality at the threshold unresolved. The record does not invent a tie rule or implementation-specific batching convention.

Sigmoid importance weights lie between zero and one and reweight regions relative to each other; they do not necessarily amplify raw activation magnitudes. The averaged attention map is a heuristic signal, not a calibrated explanation or guaranteed object mask.

No added trainable parameters does not mean zero training computation. Placement, threshold and branch probability are choices; classification and localization can trade off, and low-level maps need not capture class-specific object regions.

The source explicitly shows that attention suppression can encourage reliance on co-occurring background rather than the object. The inspected evaluation is single-object localization; broader segmentation compatibility is a proposed application, not an established universal result. No benchmark superiority or complete-object-coverage guarantee is asserted.
